learn.rule: An appositive is a short phrase that renames a noun. Put commas around it.
learn.ruleEs: Un apositivo es una frase corta que renombra un sustantivo. Pon comas a los lados.
learn.model: Venus, the hottest planet, is covered in thick clouds.
learn.notice: The words the hottest planet rename Venus. Find the two commas.

items.prompt: Which appositive renames the Moon? The Moon, ___, circles Earth.

options.text: a big bright star
Earth's natural satellite
shining at night

items.why: An appositive renames the noun with another noun phrase. The Moon is Earth's natural satellite. It is not a star, and shining at night is not a new name.
items.whyEs: Un apositivo renombra el sustantivo con otra frase nominal. La Luna es el satélite natural de la Tierra. No es una estrella, y shining at night no es un nombre nuevo.

items.prompt: Which sentence about Saturn has its commas in the right places?

options.text: Saturn, the second-largest planet, is very far away.
Saturn the second-largest planet, is very far away.
Saturn, the second-largest planet is very far away.

items.why: An appositive needs a comma before and after it. The other two are missing one.
items.whyEs: Un apositivo necesita una coma antes y otra después. A las otras dos les falta una.

items.prompt: Choose the appositive that renames Mars.
parts: , is named after a Roman god.
items.model: Mars, the red planet, is named after a Roman god.
items.why: The red planet is another name for Mars. Very cold and in space do not rename it.
items.whyEs: The red planet es otro nombre para Marte. Very cold e in space no lo renombran.

items.prompt: Check every sentence with a correctly punctuated appositive.

options.text: Venus, the hottest planet, is covered in thick clouds.
Venus the hottest planet is covered in thick clouds.
Neptune, the planet farthest from the sun, is very cold.
Neptune, the planet farthest from the sun is very cold.

items.why: The correct ones have a comma before and after the appositive. The others skip one or both commas.
items.whyEs: Las correctas tienen una coma antes y otra después del apositivo. Las otras omiten una o las dos.

items.prompt: Which sentence puts the appositive next to the noun it renames?

options.text: Ms. Garcia showed a model, our science teacher, of Saturn.
Ms. Garcia showed a model of Saturn, our science teacher.
Ms. Garcia, our science teacher, showed a model of Saturn.

items.why: Our science teacher renames Ms. Garcia, so it must sit right next to her name. In the others it lands next to the wrong words.
items.whyEs: Our science teacher renombra a Ms. Garcia, así que debe ir justo junto a su nombre. En las otras queda junto a palabras equivocadas.

items.prompt: Choose the appositive that renames the comet.

options: a ball of ice and dust
parts.answer: a ball of ice and dust

items.model: The comet, a ball of ice and dust, has a long glowing tail.
items.why: A ball of ice and dust tells what the comet is, so it renames it.
items.whyEs: A ball of ice and dust dice qué es el cometa, así que lo renombra.

familyTalk.en: Say a sentence about someone at home, then add who they are between two pauses: 'My brother, the tallest one, ...'

teacherTip.en: Have students read aloud and pause at each comma so they hear the appositive as extra information.
teacherTip.es: Pide que lean en voz alta y hagan una pausa en cada coma para que escuchen el apositivo como información extra.

items.prompt: Which sentence about Ellis Island puts the appositive next to the noun it renames?

items.why: A place where many immigrants arrived renames Ellis Island, so it belongs right after those words.
items.whyEs: A place where many immigrants arrived renombra Ellis Island, así que va justo después de esas palabras.
